options/options.html: Fine-tune behavior, manage your data, and tweak what GOG Enhancer injects.
Quick-set currency & VAT for common markets. You can override any field below.
(mixed) every 12 hours. You can edit any rate manually — manual edits stick until the next refresh.
Adds an estimated tax-inclusive price next to USD. Hover the converted figure to see the breakdown.
Pick a color theme. Applies to badges, tooltips, the game panel, and all era-aware cover effects. Requires "Design injection" enabled in the popup to see the cover effects.

(mixed) reads gog.com's own colors and font each time a page loads, so the extension's panels and badges blend in with whatever the site currently looks like — including after a redesign. On this page it simply follows your system's light/dark setting.

Switches injected UI text (badges, tooltips, the game panel, the tag dashboard) to a more dyslexia-friendly font stack with wider letter and line spacing. No fonts are downloaded — this only reorders which locally-installed fonts are tried first.
(mixed) shows the shortcuts. Off by default because it uses bare letter keys; it never acts while you're typing in a field or holding Ctrl / Alt / Cmd.
Compares a game's RAM requirement with the memory your browser reports. RAM only — browsers can't see your CPU, GPU or disk, and round the memory figure, so the result is a hint, not a promise.
Affects popup & options. Doesn't change the gog.com translations toggle.
Four small background jobs keep things fresh.
Tags, notes and price history live on this device. Sync settings live in your browser sync (small). Export anything you want.
(mixed) Pick a folder that Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive or Syncthing already keeps in sync. GOG Enhancer reads and writes one file in it,

(mixed) , and merges changes from every browser pointed at the same folder. It makes no network request for this — your folder is the whole transport. Tags, notes, play status, purchases, price alerts and price history sync; settings already sync through your browser account. Deletions sync too.
This browser can't pick a folder for sync (it needs the File System Access API — Chrome, Edge and Brave have it).
Asks for a passphrase on every sync (it is never stored) — worth it if your notes are private and the folder lives in a cloud service. Once a file is encrypted it stays encrypted for every browser.

Syncs whenever you open the tag dashboard and, when your browser remembers the folder permission (Chrome: choose “Allow on every visit” when it asks), every 30 minutes in the background. Where it would need to ask you something — a permission, or the passphrase of an encrypted file — it waits for you to press “Sync now” instead.
Keep dated backups in the folder
(mixed) Once a day, while the dashboard or this page is open, writes

(mixed) (your whole library and settings, without per-browser items and without the webhook address) and keeps the newest few. Encrypted if you ticked “Encrypt the sync file” — it asks for the passphrase.
Older ones are deleted from the folder. 1–60.
Knobs that help when troubleshooting. Off by default.

If something stopped working after a gog.com update, open the page that's misbehaving, then press this. It reports which of the extension's lookups (game cards, prices, title, panel position) still find what they need — the page address (no query string) and public store text only, nothing personal. Copy it into a bug report.
(mixed) debug lines to the gog.com DevTools console. Equivalent to setting
(mixed) Opt-in. Fires a system notification when a refund window has 1–2 days left, or when new wishlist items go on sale. Nothing is transmitted —

(mixed) wishlisted game that's dropped off its own tracked peak price — no need to set a threshold on each game's page individually. Only covers wishlist items you've visited at least once (that's what builds the price history to compare against). Requires desktop notifications above.
Minimum drop from a game's tracked peak price to trigger a wishlist-wide alert.
Snapshots kept per game before oldest are dropped. Default 100. Range 10–500. Higher = richer sparkline, more storage usage.

Optional. Powers the "Spending" stat card in the tag dashboard — purchases with a price logged (on the game page's Refund window section) in this same currency are compared against it. Leave the amount at 0 to turn the budget check off.

GOG Enhancer is free, open-source, and has no ads, analytics, or paid tiers. If it saves you money or time, a small contribution helps keep it maintained — entirely optional, and every feature stays free regardless.
GOG Enhancer can contact these addresses, and no others. It sends no cookies and no referrer, and no account information:
(mixed) — the pages you browse, and the public mods list once a day.
(mixed) — USD→EUR/ILS/GBP/PLN/RUB exchange rates (no key, no tracking).
(mixed) — the optional price-comparison table on a game page (only the game's title is sent).
(mixed) — GOG's own product API, asked once per game page which games a pack contains (only its numeric id is sent). Switch it off under Catalog, wishlist & library.
(mixed) — GOG's own catalog API, used only if you turn on endless scrolling, to fetch the next page of the list you're already looking at.
(mixed) The one other address it can ever contact is a webhook
(mixed) enter under Notification rules — off by default, and the browser asks your permission for that one origin. No analytics. No third-party fonts. Tags & notes never leave your machine.
